analysis_questions.question: Overall performance (aggregation): total revenue (sum of revenue) -> total_revenue; number of orders (rows in the cleaned data) -> order_count; average order value = total_revenue / order_count -> average_order_value.
Regional comparison (group comparison): total revenue per region -> revenue_north, revenue_south, revenue_east, revenue_west.

Quarterly trend in 2024 (trend): total revenue of orders dated in each calendar quarter of 2024 (Q1 = Jan-Mar, Q2 = Apr-Jun, Q3 = Jul-Sep, Q4 = Oct-Dec) -> revenue_2024_q1, revenue_2024_q2, revenue_2024_q3, revenue_2024_q4.

Year-over-year change (percentage change): total revenue of orders dated in 2023 -> revenue_2023; in 2024 -> revenue_2024; percentage change = (revenue_2024 - revenue_2023) / revenue_2023 * 100 -> revenue_yoy_change_pct, expressed as a percentage.

High-discount electronics (conditional filtering): among orders with product_category 'Electronics' and discount_pct >= 20: number of orders -> electronics_high_discount_orders; their total revenue -> electronics_high_discount_revenue.

Order revenue distribution (statistical summary) over all orders: mean -> order_revenue_mean; median -> order_revenue_median; sample standard deviation (denominator n - 1) -> order_revenue_std; minimum -> order_revenue_min; maximum -> order_revenue_max.

Customer concentration (derived step): number of distinct customer_id values -> unique_customer_count; revenue of the highest-revenue customer -> top_customer_revenue; top_customer_revenue / total revenue * 100 -> top_customer_revenue_share_pct.

cleaning_requirements: R1. Read every column of the raw CSV as text. Strip leading and trailing whitespace from every value. Treat the following values as missing (compare case-insensitively, after stripping): empty string, 'NA', 'N/A', 'null', 'None', '-'.
R2. Remove duplicate records BEFORE applying any other row filter: rows that share the same order_id are duplicates; keep only the first occurrence in raw-file order and discard the later ones.

R3. order_date: parse each value using exactly one of these formats: YYYY-MM-DD; MM/DD/YYYY (month first); DD-Mon-YYYY with an English 3-letter month abbreviation (e.g. 05-Mar-2024); YYYY/MM/DD; 'Month D, YYYY' with the full English month name (e.g. March 5, 2024). Drop rows whose order_date is missing or cannot be parsed. Write order_date as YYYY-MM-DD.

R4. region: map case-insensitively to one of North, South, East, West; the single-letter abbreviations N, S, E, W map to North, South, East, West. Drop rows whose region is missing or not one of these.

R5. product_category: map case-insensitively to one of Electronics, Clothing, Home & Garden, Sports, Books. Also map these variants (case-insensitive): 'Electronic' -> Electronics; 'Home and Garden' and 'Home&Garden' -> Home & Garden; 'Sport' -> Sports; 'Apparel' -> Clothing; 'Book' -> Books. Drop rows whose product_category is missing or maps to none of the five categories.

R6. unit_price: remove the substrings '$', 'USD' and ',' and surrounding spaces, then parse as a number. Drop rows whose unit_price is missing, not a number, <= 0, or > 5000. Keep the value as given (raw prices have at most 2 decimals).
R7. quantity: parse as a number (values such as '3.0' are allowed). Drop rows whose quantity is missing, not a number, not a whole number, < 1, or > 50. Store quantity as an integer.

R8. discount_pct: remove a trailing '%' and parse as a number (it is a percentage, e.g. 15 means 15%). A missing discount_pct means no discount: set it to 0. Drop rows whose discount_pct is not a number, < 0, or > 100.
R9. customer_id: convert to upper case. A missing customer_id is set to the string 'UNKNOWN' (the row is kept).
R10. Add column revenue = quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct / 100), rounded to 2 decimals.

R11. Output exactly these columns in this order: order_id, order_date, customer_id, region, product_category, quantity, unit_price, discount_pct, revenue. Sort rows by order_id ascending. Write a CSV with a header row and no index column; numbers are written without currency symbols, percent signs or thousands separators.
notes: SYNTHETIC data. Known raw imperfections: duplicate order_id rows (exact copies and re-formatted copies); five date formats; missing values written as '', NA, N/A, null, None or '-'; prices as strings with '$', 'USD', thousands separators and padding; quantities as '3.0' or padded; discounts with '%'; region/category case, padding, abbreviations and spelling variants; an unknown category ('Toys'); unparseable prices ('TBD'); invalid values (quantity <= 0 or > 50, negative prices, discounts < 0 or > 100); lower-case customer ids. findings.json is a flat JSON object mapping each metric_key to a number.
objective: Clean the raw retail order export and analyse 2023-2024 sales performance: overall revenue, regional differences, the 2024 quarterly trend, year-over-year growth, high-discount electronics orders, customer concentration and the distribution of order revenue, then report the verified findings to business stakeholders.
